policy_package: Rights, due process and anti-capture floor
why_now: No control proceeds without legality, necessity, proportionality, appeal, independent oversight and anti-incumbent safeguards.
evidence_basis: Rights baseline established; control effectiveness must be measured separately.
lead_actor: Courts; regulators; election authorities; independent oversight
success_metric: Appeal success; false-positive burden; speech/association costs; concentration effects
failure_mode: Safety policy becomes censorship, surveillance or incumbent protection.

policy_package: Enforce existing model transparency and systemic-risk duties
why_now: Applicable legal duties exist; methods and effect evidence remain uneven.
evidence_basis: L3 legal status; effect evidence mostly absent.
success_metric: Scope-correct compliance; incidents; independent access; rights cost
failure_mode: Voluntary methods are mislabeled as law or paperwork is coded as effectiveness.

why_now: Part 1 identifies a compositional failure mechanism that prompt-level controls miss.
evidence_basis: Project-C for purpose fragmentation; policy effect untested.
lead_actor: Agent providers; standards bodies; public procurers
success_metric: Unauthorized action; undocumented scope change; bypass cost; false positive; latency
failure_mode: Logging becomes surveillance or purpose records are spoofed.

why_now: Controlled evidence reaches E2, but not vote choice, dependency, naturalistic reach or agency transfer.
evidence_basis: E0–E2 capability/mechanism evidence; no validated democratic-harm gate.
success_metric: Attitude, persistence, low-cost action, reversal, exposure and rights costs
failure_mode: Model scores substitute for human outcomes or unsafe artifacts are over-disclosed.

policy_package: APE and MASK as diagnostics, not release gates
why_now: Both measure model signals, not human persuasion, manipulation or agency transfer.
success_metric: Reliability across model variants; correlation with human outcomes
failure_mode: A single score becomes a false-precision prohibition.

why_now: Release changes modifiability, monitoring and reversibility; no general EU open-weight licence exists.
evidence_basis: Strong inference; direct policy-effect evidence absent.
lead_actor: AI Office; repositories; providers; competition experts
success_metric: Residual risk by modality; derivative coverage; misuse; research/competition cost
failure_mode: Blanket licensing entrenches closed incumbents or pushes activity offshore.

why_now: Binding DSA scopes exist, but VLOP/VLOSE limits must be explicit.
evidence_basis: L3 legal status; causal effectiveness mixed.
success_metric: Mitigation closure; access latency; audit findings; recommender choice quality
failure_mode: Guidance is treated as law or smaller/off-platform systems disappear from analysis.

why_now: This is the clearest direct lesson from Cambridge Analytica and was underweighted in v0.2.
evidence_basis: L3 legal status plus historical governance evidence.
success_metric: Sponsor/targeting completeness; proxy-sensitive segments; repository latency; consent validity
failure_mode: Organic, proxy or conversational steering evades ad definitions.

why_now: The rules are unusually concrete and time-bound, but filing is not effectiveness.
evidence_basis: L3 legal status; outcomes not yet observable on 2026-08-11.
success_metric: Plan quality; implementation; exposure; latency; appeal; rights cost
failure_mode: Compliance documents are mistaken for impact or vote effects are inferred from virality.

why_now: Useful for impersonation and synthetic-media incidents; inadequate for truthful or conversational manipulation.
evidence_basis: Mixed component evidence and selected binding duties.
success_metric: Credential retention; authentication speed; label comprehension; correction latency
failure_mode: Provenance is stripped, warnings create false confidence, or legitimate uses are chilled.

policy_package: Assistant memory, loyalty and steering controls
why_now: This is central to agency transfer but the longitudinal and human-uptake evidence is thin.
success_metric: Conflict rate; switching; unassisted persistence; contestability; dependence; user welfare
failure_mode: Disclosure theatre or paternalistic substitution of provider values.

why_now: Agency transfer can occur inside government without manipulative content.
lead_actor: Public procurers; audit bodies; internal technical teams
success_metric: Tested exit; internal competence; supplier concentration; continuity; appeal
failure_mode: Registers become paperwork while institutions lose judgment and bargaining power.

why_now: Control over defaults, compute, cloud, models and answer layers can concentrate democratic power.
evidence_basis: Market evidence stronger than agency-transfer measurement.
lead_actor: Competition authorities; DMA/DSA authorities; public investors
success_metric: Switching; default share; source concentration; delegated decisions; cross-stack control
failure_mode: Market share is mistaken for agency transfer or structural remedies outrun evidence.

why_now: Fast incidents outpace post-election research; evidence access is a bottleneck.
evidence_basis: Operational precedent; effect varies by integration and trust.
lead_actor: Election bodies; platforms; researchers; civil society
success_metric: Evidence preservation; response latency; access; false alerts; correction reach
failure_mode: Cross-platform and closed-channel evidence remains inaccessible.

why_now: The concept may matter, but no validated threshold identifies when an assistant becomes constitutional infrastructure.
success_metric: Construct validity; procedural legitimacy; false inclusion/exclusion
failure_mode: Premature legislation freezes a vague concept or enables incumbent/state capture.
